DSO (Days Sales Outstanding) measures how long, on average, it takes your customers to pay invoices after they’re issued. It’s calculated by dividing the total open receivables by daily sales and expressing the result in days. A lower DSO means cash comes in quickly, supporting liquidity and reducing financing costs; a higher DSO signals slower collections, tying up working-capital and increasing exposure to bad-debt risk. Monitoring DSO helps you spot trends, benchmark against peers, and prioritize collection actions before cash-flow problems emerge.
